Subject: Post-call: Benchmark methodology & performance SLO follow-up

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to align on workload characteristics. Quick recap + next steps so we have a shared starting point for the benchmark methodology exchange.

Key requirements you called out:
- Latency SLOs: target p50 ~ <80ms, preferred p95 <200ms (streaming first-byte SLA is particularly important).
- Streaming: yes — partial tokens must be delivered to the client as soon as generated (server->client first-byte measurement).
- Concurrency / throughput: typical steady-state concurrency ~3,000 concurrent users, expected peak bursts to ~6,000. Average response length ~250 tokens; long-tail up to 1,200 tokens for ordering flows.
- Availability: graceful degradation preferred (fallback model variant) rather than hard failures during spikes.

What I attached: Redwood benchmark methodology (high level) and an example eval harness doc. The attached docs outline how we define latency/throughput, the harness we run on our infra, and reproducibility notes (seed control, tokenization, prompt normalization).

Immediate asks from our side:
1) Can you share the canonical prompt sets + a representative sample of user input? (thanks Sam — you mentioned you could export these).
2) Confirm which endpoints need streaming vs non-streaming and any auth/whitelisting constraints for our test harness.
3) Are there regulatory or network restrictions (VPC, egress controls) that would prevent us from running a test against a staged endpoint in your environment?

Next steps I'd propose:
- Sam: share prompt_set export and a short note on traffic shaping (how you expect concurrency to map to client sessions).
- We'll review the prompts, adapt the harness, and propose a canary benchmark run window.

Cc'ing Rishi for pricing/technical follow-up — he can coordinate test account access.

Appreciate the prompt export — looks representative. Quick notes on the methodology and how we define the measurements so we're aligned: 

1) Latency definitions
   - Non-streaming latency: server-side generation time until final byte sent. Measured p50/p95/p99 on the server with request timestamp and final-byte timestamp.
   - Streaming (client-first-byte) latency: we measure two things:
     a) server time to first token (server-side generation start -> first byte sent)
     b) simulated client RTT: our harness can inject configurable network RTT and measure client-observed first-byte time (request -> first token delivered). We typically report both server-first-byte and client-observed-first-byte (with 50/95/99 percentiles).

2) Throughput / concurrency
   - Our harness simulates sessions with realistic inter-request timing (you indicated multiplexing; we support both multiplexed sessions and one-request-per-session modes).
   - Throughput reported as tokens/sec and requests/sec; burst tests run with a stepped concurrency profile (ramp up -> hold -> ramp down).

3) Reproducibility & seed control
   - We normalize tokenization (same BPE vocab version) and fix RNG seeds for sampling models where applicable. For quantized variants we note differences and run pairs (full precision vs quantized) to highlight any regressions in latency or quality.

4) Measurement caveats
   - Caching and prefix-KV effects: we can run cold-start vs warmed-cache cases. Please flag any identical prefixes in your prompt set you don't want to be de-duplicated.
   - Model variants / fallbacks: if you plan to exercise fallbacks, define acceptable quality deltas and fallback thresholds.

Attachments: redwood-benchmark-methodology-v1.pdf and our eval harness runbook (redwood-eval-harness-instructions.md) — the runbook includes commands to run the harness locally against a staging endpoint and a summary of the metrics we collect.

Next actions:
- Sam: confirm which prompts must be treated as 'streaming_required' (I see labels, but flagging anything extra is helpful).
- Provide IP allowlist + test key TTL (we prefer short-lived keys for staging runs).
- Decide: Redwood runbench in our infra (faster to iterate) vs you run locally with our harness (better for network parity). We're fine with either — can start with Redwood-run canary and share artifacts for you to reproduce.

I'll coordinate with Rishi to get a staging test key if you confirm allowlist. Proposed canary window: Thu 2026-09-03 10:00–12:00 PT.
